simple.meaning: שַׁיִשׁ (shayish) is a Hebrew object word meaning “white , i.e. marble .” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Chronicles 29:2. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁיִשׁ (H7893) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H7893. shayish שַׁ֫יִשׁ noun [masculine] alabaster (foreign word? Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic שַׁיְשָׁא , perhaps Assyrian šaššu ); — ׳אַבְנֵישֿׁ 1Chr 29:2 (material of temple); compare Patrick Hast. DB MARBLE .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to bleach, i.e. whiten; See 8336 .

occurrences.englishText: Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the bronze for the things of bronze, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood; also onyx stones, stones to be set, stones for inlaid work, of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and marble stones in abundance.
